section_summary: This section contains U.S. State Department correspondence from 1932 to 1939 relating to commemorative celebrations and memorial events involving Japan and the United States. Earlier documents record reciprocal agreements to discontinue official wreath-laying on war memorials, an Armistice Day goodwill visit by Tokyo Boy Scouts, and memorial tributes honoring Japanese-American relations advocate Wallace M. Alexander. The vast majority of the section centers on the March–April 1934 celebrations marking the 80th anniversary of Commodore Matthew C. Perry's 1854 Treaty of Kanagawa, featuring joint trans-Pacific radio broadcasts, civic banquets in Tokyo, Kobe, Nagoya, and Naha, and messages exchanged between American and Japanese officials and organizations.

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet noting that Despatch No. 164 from Tokyo was filed under decimal file 811.415 Ar. 5/102.
subfiles.summary: This Document File Note records Despatch No. 164 dated July 25, 1932, from the American Embassy in Tokyo. It notes that Japan accepted the British proposal of 1930 to discontinue placing wreaths on foreign war memorials, and that Japanese overseas representatives were instructed accordingly. A copy of the despatch and exchanged correspondence is noted as attached.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Despatch No. 164 regarding Participation in War Memorial Ceremonies

subfiles.about: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits diplomatic notes exchanged with Japanese Foreign Minister Count Yasuya Uchida regarding the reciprocal cessation of wreath-laying on war memorials.
subfiles.summary: In response to a State Department circular instruction of May 19, 1932, Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits copies of official notes exchanged with the Japanese Foreign Ministry. Grew's note of July 11 informed Foreign Minister Count Yasuya Uchida that American officials in Japan would desist from placing wreaths on war memorials and participating in such ceremonies on a reciprocal basis following the British proposal. Uchida's reply of July 16 confirmed receipt and stated that Japan had accepted the British proposal in 1930 and had already instructed its foreign missions accordingly.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 164 from Tokyo on Discontinuing Participation in War Memorial Ceremonies

subfiles.about: State Department official Maxwell M. Hamilton advises against issuing a press release based on the Tokyo Boy Scouts' Armistice Day address.
subfiles.summary: This handwritten note from Maxwell M. Hamilton to Stanley K. Hornbeck discusses Tokyo Despatch No. 191 concerning the Japanese Boy Scouts. Hamilton notes that while the scouts' visit might be made the basis of a press release, he favors taking no official action.
subfiles.title: Handwritten Note on Proposed Press Release for Boy Scouts' Armistice Day Address

subfiles.about: A memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 191 regarding the visit of Japanese Boy Scouts to the American Embassy on Armistice Day.
subfiles.summary: The Division of Far Eastern Affairs summarizes Despatch No. 191 of November 12, 1932, from Tokyo. The memorandum notes that fourteen Boy Scouts of Tokyo called at the American Embassy on Armistice Day to present a short goodwill address. The Embassy viewed the gesture as evidence that the youth of Japan were not completely self-centered.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 191

subfiles.about: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reports that fourteen Boy Scouts of Tokyo visited the Embassy on Armistice Day and presented an address of goodwill to American youth.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reports that on Armistice Day, fourteen Japanese Boy Scouts representing the Boy Scouts of Tokyo called at the Embassy and presented a goodwill address. Grew notes the incident indicates that Japanese youth consider themselves part of the international youth community rather than completely self-centered. The enclosed address, signed by Kiyota Hashimoto of the Seinan Boy Scouts in Aoyama, expresses a desire to preserve world peace and offers sincere goodwill to American youth.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 191 from Tokyo Reporting Armistice Day Address by Japanese Boy Scouts

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet recording Despatch No. 1461 concerning memorial services in Japan honoring victims of the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake.
subfiles.summary: This Document File Note records Despatch No. 1461 of September 5, 1936, from Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville in Japan. The despatch was cross-referenced to decimal file 894.48 B/539. It relates to memorial services held in honor of the victims of the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Despatch No. 1461 on Memorial Services for 1923 Earthquake Victims

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet recording a request by Mrs. Bess Bettelheim Pratt for a letter of introduction to attend a missionary commemoration in the Ryukyu Islands.
subfiles.summary: This Document File Note cross-references a letter dated May 21, 1937, from Mrs. Bess Bettelheim Pratt, filed under decimal file 032 Pratt, Bess B./1. The letter concerned a celebration in the Loo Choo (Ryukyu) Islands commemorating the arrival of Bernard John Bettelheim, who established the first Christian mission there. Mrs. Pratt requested a letter of introduction from the Department of State to facilitate her attendance.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Letter from Mrs. Bess Bettelheim Pratt on Ryukyu Celebration

subfiles.about: The U.S. Maritime Commission requests the State Department to obtain six sets of a Japanese souvenir shipbuilding report commemorating Japan's 2600th anniversary.
subfiles.summary: H. L. Vickery, Assistant to the Chairman of the United States Maritime Commission, writes to Secretary of State Cordell Hull regarding Japan's upcoming twenty-six hundredth national anniversary. Having learned that Japan planned to publish a comprehensive souvenir shipbuilding report for the occasion, the Commission asks the Department to secure six sets for its technical files.
subfiles.title: Letter from Maritime Commission Requesting Japanese Souvenir Shipbuilding Report

subfiles.about: Assistant Secretary of State George S. Messersmith promises to endeavor to obtain the requested Japanese shipbuilding reports for the Maritime Commission.
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary of State George S. Messersmith writes to Rear Admiral Emory S. Land, Chairman of the Maritime Commission, acknowledging H. L. Vickery's letter of April 17. Messersmith confirms that the State Department will attempt to obtain six copies of the souvenir shipbuilding report being published in Japan for its twenty-six hundredth anniversary in 1940. He promises to forward the reports to the Commission as soon as they become available.
subfiles.title: Letter from State Department to Maritime Commission on Japanese Shipbuilding History

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State instructs the American Ambassador in Tokyo to obtain six copies of an eight-volume Japanese shipbuilding history for the Maritime Commission.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull sends Instruction No. 1711 to the American Ambassador in Tokyo regarding an eight-volume history of Japanese shipbuilding prepared by the Japan Shipbuilding Association, as reported by the American Consul at Kobe. The Ambassador is directed to arrange the acquisition of six copies of the report for the United States Maritime Commission and to inform the Department of any costs involved.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1711 to Tokyo Embassy Requesting Japanese Shipbuilding Reports

subfiles.about: Chargé d'Affaires Eugene H. Dooman reports that the Japan Shipbuilding Association's history is restricted under wartime laws and cannot be furnished to foreigners.
subfiles.summary: Chargé d'Affaires a.i. Eugene H. Dooman replies to Instruction No. 1711, stating that the requested shipbuilding study cannot be obtained. Inquiries with the Japan Shipbuilding Association (Zosen Kyokai) in Tokyo revealed that while the first two volumes had been printed and distributed to members, the works were not for sale and were restricted to members only. Dooman explains that wartime secrecy laws enacted in Japan during the hostilities in China strictly prohibit the dissemination of such technical information to foreign entities.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3956 from Tokyo on Unavailability of Japan Shipbuilding Association Report

subfiles.about: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reports on a high-level memorial service held in Tokyo for Wallace M. Alexander and transmits texts of commemorative addresses.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew describes an impressive memorial service held at the Tokyo Union Church on December 13, 1939, honoring the late Wallace McKinney Alexander, a prominent champion of American-Japanese friendship. The service was attended by leading Japanese figures, including Foreign Minister Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura, Viscount Kikujiro Ishii, Baron Yoshiro Sakatani, Mr. Yoshiaki Hatta, and Count Aisuke Kabayama. Grew observes that Japanese leaders utilized the occasion to make gestures of goodwill amid deteriorating bilateral relations, while still noting lingering Japanese resentment over the 1924 U.S. Immigration Act. Transmitted enclosures include Grew's address extolling Alexander's lifelong dedication to peace and Admiral Nomura's tribute expressing sorrow over Alexander's passing in Honolulu.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4560 from Tokyo on Memorial Service for Wallace McKinney Alexander

subfiles.about: A Department of State case jacket establishing decimal file 894.415-Perry for records concerning the 80th anniversary celebration of Commodore Perry's treaty.
subfiles.summary: This archival jacket marks the creation of decimal case subfile 894.415-Perry on March 28, 1934. The jacket designates records pertaining to the commemorative celebration of the first treaty between the United States and Japan negotiated by Commodore Matthew C. Perry. It includes standard archival handling notices and routing stamps.
subfiles.title: Case Number Jacket: 894.415-Perry

subfiles.about: The Division of Protocol returns Tokyo Telegram No. 59 to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, noting that necessary action had already been taken.
subfiles.summary: Richard Southgate of the Division of Protocol returns Tokyo Telegram No. 59 of March 28 to Dr. Stanley K. Hornbeck, Chief of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs. Southgate notes that the telegram reached Protocol late the previous afternoon and that because Far Eastern Affairs had already taken appropriate action, no further protocol review was necessary.
subfiles.title: Division of Protocol Memorandum Returning Tokyo Telegram No. 59

subfiles.about: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew inquires whether an American destroyer might convey him to Shimoda for the 80th anniversary celebration of the Perry treaty.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reports that special exercises will take place at Shimoda on April 22 to celebrate the 80th anniversary of Commodore Perry's treaty. Because the overland route to Shimoda is difficult, and with an American destroyer squadron scheduled to visit Yokohama, suggestions were made that Grew travel to Shimoda aboard an American destroyer with naval escort. With the concurrence of the Naval Attaché, Grew asks whether the Department would approve requesting the Japanese government to grant permission, emphasizing that Shimoda is not in a fortified area.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 59 from Tokyo on Proposed Destroyer Visit to Shimoda for Perry Celebration

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull instructs Ambassador Grew not to request permission for an American warship visit to the closed port of Shimoda.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull replies to Ambassador Grew's Telegram No. 59 regarding the proposed naval trip to Shimoda. Hull points out that Shimoda is not an open port and that visiting it would require special permission from the Japanese government. The Department instructs Grew not to request or indicate any desire for such permission, though it would consider the matter if Japan were to issue an unsolicited invitation.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 40 to Tokyo Declining Destroyer Request for Shimoda Visit

subfiles.about: Yomiuri Shimbun correspondent Yasuo Fuwa requests commemorative statements from Secretary of State Hull and Navy Secretary Swanson for a special Perry edition.
subfiles.summary: Yasuo Fuwa, New York correspondent for the Yomiuri Shimbun, writes to Secretary of State Cordell Hull on behalf of publisher Matsutaro Shoriki. He requests a commemorative statement to the Japanese people for a special edition celebrating the 80th anniversary of Commodore Perry's arrival in Japan. Fuwa emphasizes the newspaper's liberal tradition and notes that such a statement would reinforce recent cordial exchanges between Hull and Foreign Minister Koki Hirota. Fuwa encloses a copy of a parallel appeal addressed to Secretary of the Navy Claude A. Swanson.
subfiles.title: Letter from Yasuo Fuwa Requesting Perry Anniversary Statements from Hull and Swanson

subfiles.about: The State Department declines to provide an exclusive anniversary message to the Yomiuri Shimbun, citing official policy against non-standard channels.
subfiles.summary: Richard Southgate, Assistant Chief of the Division of Protocol and Conferences, replies to Yasuo Fuwa's letter to Secretary Hull. Southgate acknowledges the appropriateness of commemorating the 80th anniversary of Commodore Perry's Treaty of Peace and Amity, praising the enduring friendship between the two nations. However, he explains that Secretary Hull cannot comply with publisher Shoriki's request because Department policy prohibits releasing public messages abroad through non-official channels.
subfiles.title: Letter from State Department Declining Yomiuri Shimbun Statement Request

subfiles.about: Under Secretary of State William Phillips informs Navy Secretary Claude A. Swanson of the Department's response to the Yomiuri Shimbun's request.
subfiles.summary: Under Secretary of State William Phillips writes to Secretary of the Navy Claude A. Swanson regarding the solicitations received from Yasuo Fuwa of the Yomiuri Shimbun. Phillips notes that Fuwa sought anniversary statements from both departments for the Perry commemoration. He transmits a copy of the State Department's reply declining the request, emphasizing that public statements for foreign dissemination should follow regular diplomatic channels.
subfiles.title: Letter from State Department to Secretary of the Navy regarding Yomiuri Shimbun Request

subfiles.about: A protocol memorandum analyzing a telegram received from the Kobe Chamber of Commerce and submitting a draft reply.
subfiles.from: Division of International Conferences and Protocol
subfiles.summary: The Division of International Conferences and Protocol forwards a telegram from the Kobe Chamber of Commerce to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs. The drafter observes that despite awkward English phrasing touching upon military affairs, the intent of the Kobe Chamber is manifestly peaceful. A draft reply for Secretary Hull is submitted for review and comment.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Kobe Chamber of Commerce Perry Anniversary Telegram

subfiles.about: The Kobe Chamber of Commerce sends an anniversary greeting celebrating 80 years of trade and peace since Perry's treaty.
subfiles.from: Kobe Chamber of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.summary: The Kobe Chamber of Commerce telegraphs Secretary of State Cordell Hull on the eightieth anniversary of the first U.S.-Japan treaty. The message acknowledges Japan's debt to America in developing its industry and civilization and emphasizes that despite contradictions in military affairs, Japan's peace-loving spirit will foster Pacific peace. It adds that the local American Consul was invited to an anniversary dinner in honor of the occasion.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Kobe Chamber of Commerce Commemorating Perry Treaty

subfiles.about: Under Secretary of State William Phillips reports a request from the Tokyo Asahi correspondent for a Perry anniversary statement.
subfiles.summary: Under Secretary of State William Phillips informs Far Eastern Division Chief Stanley K. Hornbeck that Takemi Shirakawa, correspondent for The Tokyo Asahi and The Osaka Asahi, called to request a statement from Secretary Hull for a special Perry edition. Phillips noted to Shirakawa the difficulty of granting an exclusive message to one newspaper but suggested considering a general Departmental release. Phillips requests a conference with Hornbeck on the matter.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo Asahi Request for Perry Anniversary Statement

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet recording an NBC inquiry regarding a State Department speaker for a Perry anniversary radio program.
subfiles.summary: This Document File Note cross-references a letter dated March 21, 1934, from the National Broadcasting Company, filed under decimal file 811.415 Perry, Matthew C./16. The letter informed the Department of a commemorative radio broadcast arranged for the anniversary of the first treaty between the United States and Japan and inquired whether a Department representative would speak on the program.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Letter from NBC on Perry Treaty Broadcast

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet recording outgoing Telegram No. 43 to Tokyo containing the Secretary's Perry anniversary statement.
subfiles.summary: This Document File Note records Telegram No. 43 sent to the American Embassy in Tokyo on March 29, 1934, at 6:00 p.m., cross-referenced to decimal file 811.415 Perry, Matthew C./18. The telegram transmitted the text of Secretary Hull's statement to the Chamber of Commerce of the United States regarding commemorative observances for Commodore Perry.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Telegram No. 43 to Tokyo Quoting Statement to U.S. Chamber of Commerce

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits the text of an upcoming press release celebrating the 80th anniversary of Commodore Perry's treaty.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to the American Embassy in Tokyo a confidential press release scheduled for publication on March 31, 1934. The release quotes Hull's March 1 letter to the Chamber of Commerce of the United States endorsing its initiative to celebrate the 80th anniversary of Commodore Perry's Treaty of Peace and Amity. Hull's statement praises the enduring foundation of friendship, the reciprocal commercial exchange between both economies, and the desire of the United States to continue peaceful and constructive cooperation with Japan. Ambassador Grew is instructed to issue the same release in Japan if no objections exist.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 43 to Tokyo Transmitting Press Release on Perry Treaty Anniversary

subfiles.about: Under Secretary of State William Phillips informs the Tokyo Asahi correspondent of the general press release on the Perry anniversary.
subfiles.summary: Under Secretary of State William Phillips sends a telegram to Takemi Shirakawa, New York correspondent for The Tokyo Asahi. Referring to Shirakawa's request for an exclusive message, Phillips states that Secretary Hull is issuing a general press statement for all morning newspapers on March 31. Phillips expresses appreciation for the paper's cordial attitude while reaffirming the Department's policy against exclusive statements, adding that an advance copy of the release is being mailed.
subfiles.title: Telegram to Tokyo Asahi Correspondent regarding Perry Anniversary Press Release

subfiles.about: An archival duplicate copy of outgoing Telegram No. 43 to Tokyo transmitting the Perry anniversary press release.
subfiles.summary: This subfile contains a duplicate record copy of Telegram No. 43 sent by Secretary of State Cordell Hull to the American Embassy in Tokyo on March 29, 1934. It contains the identical full text of Hull's press release endorsing the U.S. Chamber of Commerce's Perry commemoration and extolling Japanese-American trade and friendship, bearing Division of Far Eastern Affairs routing stamps.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 43 to Tokyo Transmitting Perry Treaty Press Release (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: An archival triplicate copy of outgoing Telegram No. 43 to Tokyo transmitting the Perry anniversary press release.
subfiles.summary: This subfile contains a third official file copy of Telegram No. 43 sent on March 29, 1934, from Secretary Hull to the Tokyo Embassy. It sets forth the full text of Hull's statement commemorating the 80th anniversary of Commodore Perry's treaty for publication in Japan and the United States.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 43 to Tokyo Transmitting Perry Treaty Press Release (Triplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: White House Secretary Louis McH. Howe refers Baron Goh's congratulatory anniversary telegram to the Secretary of State for acknowledgment.
subfiles.summary: Louis McH. Howe, Secretary to President Franklin D. Roosevelt, transmits a referral slip to Secretary of State Cordell Hull. The slip forwards a congratulatory cablegram received from Baron Seinosuke Goh, President of the Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry, for appropriate acknowledgment.
subfiles.title: White House Referral Slip Transmitting Telegram from Baron Goh

subfiles.about: Baron Seinosuke Goh sends congratulations to President Roosevelt on the 80th anniversary of Japanese-American relations.
subfiles.summary: Baron Seinosuke Goh, President of the Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry, cables President Franklin D. Roosevelt on the 80th anniversary of bilateral relations. Goh expresses heartfelt happiness and congratulations on the growing amicable and solid commercial ties between Japan and the United States. He voices confident expectation that mutual cordiality and everlasting friendship will be accelerated in the future.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Baron Goh to President Roosevelt on Perry Treaty Anniversary

subfiles.about: The Office of Coordination and Review notes a delay in handling a request from the Japanese Students' Association of Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: This memorandum from the Office of Coordination and Review comments on the internal routing of a letter from the Japanese Students' Association of Hawaii dated March 27. The note highlights that the letter arrived in FE on April 9 and Protocol on April 16, but the draft answer only reached Coordination and Review on April 18. Noting that the writer requested a reply before April 27, the memorandum questions why FE did not acknowledge the communication more promptly.
subfiles.title: Office of Coordination and Review Memorandum on Hawaii Letter Delay

subfiles.about: Isamu Sato requests a message of encouragement for a student production of a play about Townsend Harris commemorating Perry's treaty.
subfiles.summary: Isamu Sato, President of the Japanese Students' Association of Hawaii, writes to Secretary of State Cordell Hull regarding the 80th anniversary of the Perry Treaty. Sato announces that the student association will stage a play entitled 'The American Envoy' on April 27, 1934, portraying the career of Townsend Harris as the first American Consul General in Japan and guardian of Japanese-American relations. He solicits a message of goodwill and encouragement from the Secretary to promote peace and mutual understanding.
subfiles.title: Letter from Japanese Students' Association of Hawaii Requesting Goodwill Message

subfiles.about: Takemi Shirakawa thanks Under Secretary Phillips for his telegram and the Perry anniversary press release.
subfiles.summary: Takemi Shirakawa, New York correspondent for The Tokyo Asahi and The Osaka Asahi, writes to Under Secretary of State William Phillips. Shirakawa expresses sincere gratitude for Phillips' telegram of March 30 responding to his request for a special commemorative message marking the 80th anniversary of the Perry expedition.
subfiles.title: Letter from Takemi Shirakawa Thanking State Department for Press Release

subfiles.about: Secretary Hull instructs Ambassador Grew to convey his appreciation to the Kobe Chamber of Commerce for its anniversary telegram.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull instructs the American Embassy in Tokyo regarding the telegram received from the Kobe Chamber of Commerce. Hull directs Ambassador Grew to inform the Kobe Chamber of his sincere appreciation for its cordial commemorative message celebrating 80 years of treaty relations.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 44 to Tokyo Instructing Acknowledgment of Kobe Chamber Message

subfiles.about: Secretary Hull directs Ambassador Grew to acknowledge Baron Goh's congratulatory cable to President Roosevelt.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull instructs the American Embassy in Tokyo concerning Baron Seinosuke Goh's anniversary telegram to President Roosevelt. Grew is directed to convey an appropriate acknowledgment expressing that the American people sincerely reciprocate Baron Goh's friendly sentiments and share his confident expectation of enduring cordial relations.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 45 to Tokyo Instructing Acknowledgment of Baron Goh Cable

subfiles.about: A brief memorandum evaluating Ambassador Grew's commemorative addresses transmitted in Despatch No. 728.
subfiles.summary: This concise memorandum from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs reviews the two commemorative speeches delivered by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo. The evaluation remarks that the Ambassador's addresses are 'unobjectionable, but not particularly interesting.'
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Ambassador Grew's Addresses

subfiles.about: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reports extensively on 80th anniversary celebrations of the Perry Treaty and transmits speeches, press clippings, telegrams, and Okinawa reports.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reports on extensive observances held throughout Japan on March 30–31, 1934, commemorating the 80th anniversary of Commodore Perry's treaty. Grew details his participation in a joint trans-Pacific radio broadcast over JOAK with Viscount Kikujiro Ishii (accompanied in America by Ambassador Hirosi Saito and Roland S. Morris), as well as a major luncheon banquet hosted by the Tokyo and Yokohama Chambers of Commerce featuring speeches by Baron Seinosuke Goh and Vice-Minister Mamoru Shigemitsu. The despatch encloses press clippings from The Japan Times reporting these events and speeches; telegraphic greetings exchanged between Grew and the Chambers of Commerce of Kobe (Tadao Okazaki) and Nagoya (Sosuke Okaya); Grew's message to the Okinawa Nippo and citizens of Naha celebrating Perry's initial landing; and translations of Okinawa Nippo coverage of local celebrations in Naha.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 728 from Tokyo Reporting Observance of Perry Treaty 80th Anniversary

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew transmits a copy of his letter to Tadao Okazaki acknowledging the Kobe Chamber of Commerce's anniversary telegram.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew refers to Department Instruction No. 44 and transmits a copy of his official letter sent to Tadao Okazaki, President of the Kobe Chamber of Commerce and Industry. The enclosed letter, dated April 5, conveys Secretary Hull's sincere appreciation for the Chamber's cordial message on the eightieth anniversary of the first Japanese-American treaty.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Tokyo Enclosing Letter of Acknowledgment to Kobe Chamber of Commerce

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary of the Navy H. L. Roosevelt thanks the State Department for sharing its correspondence regarding the Yomiuri Shimbun request.
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Navy Henry L. Roosevelt writes to Secretary of State Cordell Hull acknowledging receipt of the Department's letter of March 28 and enclosed copy of its reply to Yasuo Fuwa of the Yomiuri Shimbun. Roosevelt expresses the Navy Department's appreciation for being kept informed regarding the commemorative requests for the Perry anniversary.
subfiles.title: Letter from Navy Department Acknowledging State Department Action on Yomiuri Request

subfiles.about: Kansai civic bodies express gratitude for 80 years of Japanese-American friendship and prosperous commercial relations.
subfiles.from: Japan America Society Kansai and Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.summary: The Japan America Society Kansai and the Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry send a joint cablegram to Secretary of State Cordell Hull. On the occasion of the 80th anniversary of the first U.S.-Japan treaty, they express profound gratitude for the historically friendly and increasingly prosperous trade relations between both nations, voicing sincere hope that their traditional friendship will continue to strengthen.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Kansai Japan America Society and Osaka Chamber Commemorating Treaty

subfiles.about: The Division of Protocol submits a tailored draft reply to Isamu Sato for review by Far Eastern Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Richard Southgate of the Division of Protocol writes to Maxwell M. Hamilton of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs regarding the communication from Isamu Sato of the Japanese Students' Association of Hawaii. Southgate notes that because such letters require varied treatment, no stereotyped acknowledgment exists. Protocol submits an individual draft reply for FE's consideration.
subfiles.title: Division of Protocol Memorandum on Replying to Japanese Students' Association

subfiles.about: Maxwell M. Hamilton routes the proposed reply to Isamu Sato to Protocol for further handling.
subfiles.summary: This brief handwritten note initialed by Maxwell M. Hamilton ('m. m. H.') of Far Eastern Affairs routes the draft reply to the Japanese Students' Association of Hawaii to the Protocol Division, suggesting that Protocol review and finalize the acknowledgment.
subfiles.title: Handwritten Routing Note on Draft Letter to Japanese Students' Association

subfiles.about: Eugene H. Dooman explains that the play 'The American Envoy' contained scurrilous depictions of Townsend Harris, warranting a minimal acknowledgment.
subfiles.summary: Eugene H. Dooman of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs drafts an explanatory memorandum regarding the play 'The American Envoy' mentioned by the Japanese Students' Association of Hawaii. Dooman observes that when the play was staged in Japan several years earlier, it caused a sensation by making scurrilous and unnecessary digressions into the private life of Townsend Harris. He notes that the Department's draft acknowledgment was deliberately drafted to say no more than strictly necessary.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on 'The American Envoy' Play

subfiles.about: The State Department politely declines to provide a separate message for the Hawaiian student performance of 'The American Envoy'.
subfiles.summary: Richard Southgate, Assistant Chief of the Division of Protocol and Conferences, replies on behalf of Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Isamu Sato, President of the Japanese Students' Association of Hawaii. Acknowledging Sato's letter of March 27 regarding the student presentation of 'The American Envoy', Southgate states that while the Secretary is deeply interested in promoting international goodwill, he has already publicly articulated his sentiments on the 80th anniversary of Commodore Perry's treaty. Consequently, Southgate explains that it would not be appropriate for the Secretary to renew expressions of sentiment for the theatrical event.
